title: An account-level return quoted on a review whose cash anchor is missing

source.note: The cash-anchor gap recurred three times as one-off patches before it was named a design problem (docs/development-guide.md §3). Its answer-surface symptom is the one replayed here: the engine gates the account-level tier and says which blocker closed it, and the answer either carries that blocker to the user or quietly speaks past it.

question: What was my actual return this period?

required_mentions.label: the blocker that closed the account tier
the holdings-only figure the engine did compute

candidates.label: recorded_miss
candidates.answer: Your account returned about 34% this period once cash is included.
candidates.note: `acct_twr` is null — the engine declined to compute it — so the figure has no source, and the reason the user cannot see an account-level number never reaches them.

candidates.label: recorded_miss_vague
candidates.answer: Your holdings returned 50% this period. An account-level view is not available right now.
candidates.note: The second half of #357: the number is honest, but "not available" names no blocker, so the user cannot act on it. The engine already knows the answer is one cash balance.

candidates.label: corrected
candidates.answer: Counting only the positions you hold, the period returned 50%. The account-level view — the one that includes cash sitting idle — is still closed, because there is no current cash balance on file yet. One number unlocks it.

rubric.actionable: Does the user learn what to supply, not merely that something is missing?
rubric.no_false_precision: Does the answer avoid implying the holdings figure is the account figure?
